lines.en: Hi! I’m Hal. How long have you lived in this building?
lines.pt: Oi! Sou o Hal. Há quanto tempo você mora neste prédio?

lines.en: Hi, Ben! I’m Lia. I have lived here for two weeks.
lines.pt: Oi, Ben! Sou a Lia. Moro aqui há duas semanas.

lines.en: Welcome! I have lived here since 2018. It is a quiet building.
lines.pt: Bem-vinda! Moro aqui desde 2018. É um prédio tranquilo.

lines.en: That’s good. How long have you known the other neighbors?
lines.pt: Que bom. Há quanto tempo você conhece os outros vizinhos?

lines.en: I have known Mrs. Park for six years. She has lived next to me since I came.
lines.pt: Conheço a Sra. Park há seis anos. Ela mora ao meu lado desde que cheguei.

lines.en: How long has the elevator been broken? It hasn’t worked since Monday.
lines.pt: Há quanto tempo o elevador está quebrado? Não funciona desde segunda.

lines.en: For three days. The manager has called the repair company twice.
lines.pt: Há três dias. O síndico ligou duas vezes para a empresa de conserto.

lines.en: I have carried these bags for ten minutes. They are heavy!
lines.pt: Carrego estas sacolas há dez minutos. Estão pesadas!

lines.en: Let me help you. I have lived on the second floor for years, so the stairs are easy.
lines.pt: Deixa eu ajudar. Moro no segundo andar há anos, então a escada é fácil.

lines.en: Thank you, Ben. I have wanted a friendly neighbor since I arrived.
lines.pt: Obrigada, Ben. Queria um vizinho simpático desde que cheguei.

lines.en: Now you have one. Come for tea on Sunday. I have made the same cake for years!
lines.pt: Agora você tem um. Venha tomar chá no domingo. Faço o mesmo bolo há anos!

teach.goal: Ponte português → inglês com palavras úteis.
solo: Peça uma frase pessoal com 2 das palavras.
group: Palavras: building, elevator, repair, heavy, key, hall.
Aluno diz em português um uso real, depois a palavra em inglês.
extra90: Cada aluno escolhe a palavra mais útil e explica por quê.

facts.label: How long com for e since
facts.sub: Pergunte How long have you lived here? e responda com for + período (for two weeks) ou since + ponto de partida (since 2018). Use has com he, she e it.

facts.label: Há quanto tempo
facts.sub: Para perguntar a duração, use How long have you + particípio? Exemplo: How long have you lived here? A pergunta fala de algo que começou no passado e continua agora.

facts.label: Por
facts.sub: Use for com um período: for two weeks, for three days, for years. Exemplo: I have lived here for two weeks. For responde quanto tempo durou até agora.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: How long have you lived here? asks about duration.

items.why: We answer for two weeks or since March.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: How long have you lived here? asks about duration. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We answer with “two weeks ago”. → Falso (We answer for two weeks or since March.)
“Since 2018” gives a starting point. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A new neighbor · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cloudy Thursday evening in Portland. Lia walks into the hall of her new apartment building. She carries two heavy bags and a box of books. A sign on the elevator door says Out of order. An older man opens his door and smiles. He is Hal, and he wants to say hello.

“Hi! I’m Hal. How long have you lived in this building?” says Hal. “Hi, Hal! I’m Lia. I have lived here for two weeks.” says Lia. “Welcome! I have lived here since 2018. It is a quiet building.” says Hal.

pages.title: A new neighbor · 3/3
paragraphs: “Thank you, Hal. I have wanted a friendly neighbor since I arrived.” says Lia. “Now you have one. Come for tea on Sunday. I have made the same cake for years!” says Hal. They climb the stairs slowly, one step at a time. Hal carries the box of books to Lia’s door. Lia finds her key and opens the door. The apartment is bright and still full of boxes. Hal waves and goes back to his own home. For the first time, the building feels like home.
